assumptions.assumption: The issue's named seam (agent/guardian/delta_emitter.py) is not the right one and was not used.
assumptions.rationale: The agent/ Python tree is retired. Its live descendant ts/src/guardian/delta-emitter.ts serializes the api-delta.json endpoint contract and has no coverage concept. The real seam is the diff-coverage ladder (report-tier.ts + orchestrator.ts), which is what this change extends.
assumptions.default: Built ts/src/guardian/diff-coverage/coverage-delta.ts as a leaf of that package.

assumptions.assumption: A regression is a drop in the whole-file covered ratio, not a per-line 'was hit, now unhit' comparison.
assumptions.rationale: A diff shifts line numbers, so base line N and head line N are not the same line; a line-identity rule would manufacture findings out of an insertion.
assumptions.default: ratio = covered/coverable per file per report; regression when the drop exceeds 0.1 percentage points (float-noise guard).

assumptions.assumption: A file whose report record has zero coverable lines is skipped, not scored.
assumptions.rationale: 0/0 is a ratio guardian would be inventing. Consistent with the ladder never grading a unit it could not measure.
assumptions.default: Excluded from deltas AND from unitsCompared, so it lowers the denominator loudly rather than passing quietly.

assumptions.assumption: A coverage regression is graded HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW by percentage points lost (>=20 / >=5 / >0) and NEVER CRITICAL.
assumptions.rationale: An uncovered new block is a fact about one artifact; a drop is a relative measurement across two artifacts guardian cannot verify are genuinely base-and-head of the same PR. The top of the scale stays reserved for what guardian proves alone.
assumptions.default: Regressions are ordinary findings; the configured gate (soft/hard) decides whether they block, exactly like every other guardian finding. No new blocking rule was added.

assumptions.assumption: The head-only degradation notice fires on EVERY pr-check run that judged units without a base artifact, including runs that never asked for a delta.
assumptions.rationale: Pre-answered in the issue's accepted-risk section: 'degrade to delta unavailable - head-only with a LOUD note when no base artifact is present. Do not silently pass.' A notice gated on opting in would make the silent case the default, which is the exact failure the issue names.
assumptions.consequence: Two existing fixtures asserted 'nothing is degraded' on runs that supply --coverage but no base report. Both were amended to supply a base report so they remain genuine non-degraded cases — the assertions were NOT relaxed. This mirrors the amendment #554 already made to the same guardian-cli.test.ts fixture for the same reason one level up.
assumptions.reviewNote: This is the one judgement call in the change and the thing to review first: until base-coverage artifacts are wired into CI, every guardian pr-check run gains one ::warning:: line.

assumptions.assumption: The archived analysis record's schema stays at 1.3; the delta is not added to it.
assumptions.rationale: Extending that record is a schema-versioned change with its own consumers. The delta reaches machine consumers through the --format json surface's additive coverage_delta block.
assumptions.default: Out of scope; noted in the plan as a follow-up.

assumptions.assumption: The delta is wired to pr-check only, not to author-plan or analyze.
assumptions.rationale: A base-vs-head comparison is a PR-time question; author-plan has no base ref to compare against.
A worktree under .claude/ breaks the pre-push check-docs gate, which self-excludes that path and then scans zero files — a zero denominator reporting as a pass.
assumptions.default: Sibling worktree of the main checkout.
